text:
Sam: Quick check — planning to change /v1/generate structured responses to always set Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 and to return explicit `null` for optional fields instead of omitting them. PR #1428. Will this break client libs that expect fields to be absent?

Jess: Strong preference to avoid surface-breaking changes. Can we do a header-based opt-in first? `X-Redwood-Response-Version: 2` maybe.

Kai: Is the change just for non-streaming responses or also affects ndjson streaming chunks? Need to confirm since streaming clients parse line-by-line.

Sam: Good point — plan right now targets non-streaming structured outputs only. Streaming will keep the same chunk format for now.

Anita: If we must return `null`, SDKs should probably normalize `null` -> `undefined` for optional fields to remain tolerant. That would be low risk.

Sam: Agreed. My concern is third-party clients that do manual JSON access might treat `null` differently.

Jess: Another mitigation: add response header `X-Redwood-Compat: v2` so servers can flip on version for a canary subset. That avoids default breakage.

Kai: I can send a small SDK patch that tolerates both missing and null for optional typed fields. Will target node & browser SDKs.

sdk-ci-bot: CI update: js-sdk unit tests failing (2 tests) in main branch referencing omitted-field behavior.

Sam: Thanks — Kai, assign the SDK PR to me for quick review. I'll also add a short canary rollout plan: 5% hosted traffic -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours if no regressions.

Jess: Small request: include an example in the PR description showing old vs new responses, and add a migration note in the changelog.

Sam: Example (non-streaming):
``` 
// old
{
  "choices": [ { "text": "ok" } ]
}
// new
{
  "choices": [ { "text": "ok", "metadata": null } ]
}
```

Kai: I'll update tests to accept either form and add an explicit assertion for the header `X-Redwood-Response-Version` during canary.

Anita: Also add e2e that runs the browser SDK parsing path; that's where we saw flaky behavior last time.

Sam: Timeline: Kai will open SDK PR today, I'll merge the API change behind the header flag once SDK passes, then enable 5% canary tomorrow morning. If no significant errors after 24h, ramp to 25%.

Jess: @Sam can you post the canary dashboard link when it's live so folks can eyeball 5xx/latency/parse-errors quickly? :eyes:

Sam: Will do. Thanks everyone — tagging this resolved for now, will update thread with PR links.

Kai: PR opened: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1432 - includes tests and a compatibility toggle.

sdk-ci-bot: CI: PR 1432 — all checks green on node 18, flaky browser test retried.

Sam: Merge done. Canary scheduled at 06:00 UTC tomorrow.

Anita: Great, I'll watch e2e.

Jess: Thanks all.
